contentHtml:
How to get to Xilitla is one of the most common questions from people planning their first visit to the Huasteca Potosina. Xilitla is a mountain town tucked into the Sierra Madre Oriental in San Luis Potosí, famous for Edward James's Sculpture Garden and its jungle waterfalls. Knowing how to get to Xilitla from your starting city saves hours on the road and keeps you off unnecessary detours.

This guide breaks down the road route from Mexico City, Monterrey and the city of San Luis Potosí, including distances, real travel times, transportation options and current costs. In 2026, admission to the Sculpture Garden costs $180 MXN for adults at the ticket office, something worth knowing before you set out. You'll also find advice on timing, services along the way and links to help you plan each leg of the trip.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: October 2026. Before you go, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina to make the most of every day.

Road routes to Xilitla: real distances and travel times

How do you get to Xilitla from Mexico City?

The most direct road route from Mexico City to Xilitla covers about 350 km (217 miles) and takes around 7 h by car. It follows Federal 85 through Pachuca to Tamazunchale and then takes the Federal 120 turnoff to Xilitla. The drive combines toll highway with two-lane stretches through the hills.

Travelers usually leave before 5:00 a.m. to arrive in daylight and avoid driving the mountain stretches at night. The last stretch from Tamazunchale has sharp curves, but the pavement is in good condition in 2026. Book a tour to Xilitla if you'd rather travel as a group with transportation included.

Route from Monterrey: the fastest option from the north

From Monterrey the distance is about 500 km, with an estimated time of ~7 h. The route takes the Monterrey–Ciudad Victoria highway (Federal 85N), continues to Ciudad Mante and reaches Ciudad Valles, from where you continue south on Federal 85 and take Federal 120 to Xilitla. That final stretch takes about an hour and a half because of the curves.

If you're taking public transportation from Monterrey, catch a bus to Ciudad Valles with Omnibus de México or Futura, and from the bus station take a shared taxi (taxi colectivo) to Xilitla. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina departing from Ciudad Valles.

How do you get to Xilitla from the city of San Luis Potosí and other cities?

From the city of San Luis Potosí: the shortest route in time

From the city of San Luis Potosí, the state capital, it's 310 km to Xilitla, and the drive takes about 5 h. Take Federal 70 to Rioverde and from there the route through Jalpan to Xilitla: it doesn't go through Ciudad Valles. The rainy season, from June to September, can cause minor landslides on the final mountain stretch, so check road conditions before you leave. Check the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina and plan your departure with time to spare.

Transportation and admission costs in 2026

A bus ticket from Ciudad Valles to Xilitla costs $80 to $120 MXN, depending on the bus line. A private taxi from Ciudad Valles runs about $1,200 MXN per vehicle. If you'd rather go with a guide, the Surrealist Route (Ruta Surrealista), which tours Edward James's Las Pozas with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles (from Valles, $400 MXN more per booking), breakfast, admission and a certified guide, costs $1,400 MXN per person.

There are no online ticket sales for now: you book your time slot for free in the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. Admission is $180 MXN for adults and $120 MXN for children ages 6 to 12 and adults over 65; kids under 6 get in free. A guide is mandatory: $30 MXN per person in Spanish and $60 MXN in another language. The garden is open Wednesday through Monday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:00 p.m.; it's closed on Tuesdays. Arrive 10 minutes early: if you're late, you lose your slot. If you see $170 MXN on other sites, that was the online price in early 2026. Get all the details in our Las Pozas ticket guide to skip the lines.

Tips before you hit the road to Xilitla

  • Leave early in the morning: the mountain stretch between Ciudad Valles and Xilitla is safe by day. Arriving before 4:00 p.m. is essential if you want to get into the Garden: that's last entry, even though it closes at 6:00 p.m.
  • Book your time slot online: booking is free and you can do it up to 60 days ahead; you pay admission at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit. See our Las Pozas ticket guide.
  • Plan your lodging: in high season the guesthouses downtown fill up fast. The 3-day Xilitla itinerary includes lodging options and activities organized by day.
  • Pack the right clothes: humidity in Xilitla is above 80% most of the year. Wear light clothing, bring a rain jacket and shoes with good grip for the Garden's paths.

Frequently asked questions about getting to Xilitla

How long does it take to get to Xilitla from Mexico City?

The trip from Mexico City takes about 7 h by car on Federal 85, via Pachuca, to Tamazunchale and then Federal 120. By public transportation it can stretch to 9 to 10 hours, counting transfers in Tamazunchale or Ciudad Valles in 2026.

How much is admission to the Sculpture Garden in Xilitla in 2026?

Admission is $180 MXN for adults, paid at the garden's ticket office on the day of your visit after booking your time slot for free in the official system; there are no online sales for now. Children ages 6 to 12 and adults 65 and older pay $120 MXN. Kids under 6 and local residents with ID get in free.

How do you get to Xilitla from San Luis Potosí without a car?

Take a bus from the city of San Luis Potosí to Ciudad Valles (~3 h, with Omnibus de México or Futura), and from the Ciudad Valles bus station catch a shared taxi (colectivo) to Xilitla for about $100 MXN. The colectivo leaves when all the seats are filled, usually within 20 minutes.

Is the road to Xilitla safe for families?

The road is open year-round and suitable for families. It's best to avoid driving the stretch between Ciudad Valles and Xilitla at night because of the mountain curves. In the rainy season, check road conditions before you leave. Public transportation is also a safe and affordable option when traveling with kids.
